text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of this Midlands derby from the Premier League, as Aston Villa make the short trip to Molineux to face Wolves!

While neither club sees this game as their biggest local tussle, West Bromwich Albion and Birmingham City's absence from the Premier League means there is still plenty at stake here! Gary O'Neil's Wolves approach the game in positive spirits after Hwang Hee-chan's goal made them the first team to beat Manchester City this season, taking them to seven points from seven matches to start the campaign.
With all three promoted teams and Bournemouth losing on Saturday, this represents a chance to put a buffer between themselves and those at the bottom of the table.
Aston Villa, meanwhile, recorded a memorable victory of their own last week as Ollie Watkins' hat-trick helped them thrash Brighton 6-1, their 10th consecutive Premier League win at Villa Park.
Taking that form on the road is the challenge now for Villa, who needed a stoppage-time strike from John McGinn to overcome Zrinjski Mostar in the Europa Conference League on Thursday.
Villa have so far failed to beat Wolves under Unai Emery, drawing once and losing once – can they end that hoodoo here?
Wolves are unchanged from last week's win over the champions, for which O'Neil reverted to a back three.
Toti, who got the winner in this exact fixture in May as Julen Lopetegui's Wolves made certain of Premier League survival, keeps his place alongside Kilman and Dawson.
The only alteration comes on the bench, where City loanee Doyle replaces Joe Hodge.
Jean-Ricner Bellegarde serves the last game of his three-match ban.
Having rotated for Villa's midweek win in Europe, Emery makes six changes to his lineup for this one.
Last week's hat-trick hero Watkins joins Cash, Luiz, Torres, Kamara and Diaby – who has overcome a knock – in returning to the team.
Lenglet, Bailey, Tielemans, Zaniolo, Duran and former Wolves man Dendoncker all drop to the bench.
It looks like Emery might match Wolves' 3-4-3 shape here, though it could be that Cash plays a more advanced role – we'll find out soon enough!
Across every team's last 20 Premier League games ahead of matchday eight, only Manchester City (52) won more points than Aston Villa's 42 (W13 D3 L4).
Will they maintain their strong run here, or will the formbook go out of the window on derby day? We're about to find out – kick-off is fast approaching!
We're under way in the Molineux sunshine as Wolves get the ball rolling on derby day!
Kilman finds the run of Semedo with a lovely floated ball down the right, and the wing-back is supported by Neto.
However, McGinn blocks his initial cross and Wolves fail to make anything of the resulting throw-in.
Villa, donning their white away kit, are put under pressure as Hwang chases a pass back to Martinez.
The World Cup winner finds Konsa on the right, who draws a foul from Cunha.
Villa win the first corner of the game as Digne gets down the left to cross, and the bouncing ball is headed behind by Ait-Nouri with Cash lurking at the far post.
Digne goes short to Diaby after the referee has a word with Lemina and Torres, who were wrestling inside the six-yard box.
Diaby's cross is flicked towards Torres at the back, but he's caught offside as he struggles to keep the ball in play.
Luiz looks to turn Toti on the edge of the box, but the Wolves man wins the ball to initiate a counter-attack.
Kamara pulls Cunha back on halfway and receives the game's first yellow card.
GREAT SAVE! Villa should be 1-0 up as McGinn floats a cross over to Cash, who is attacking the far post.
He meets it with a well-struck volley, but Sa is equal to it to turn it past his near post!
Close! The corner is worked short again, and Diaby's cross is cleared as far as McGinn.
He takes aim from 30 yards out, and his strike barely whistles past Sa's left-hand post.
That was a close call!
Villa look to have started with a back four when in possession, with Cash pushing high and Konsa covering for the Poland international at right-back.
It's a flexible system, however, so we'll see if it changes as the game progresses.
McGinn is fortunate to avoid being penalised for a challenge on Semedo, as he looked to have a handful of the wing-back's shirt as he slid in to win a throw-in.
The ball is swiftly recovered by Wolves, however.
The early exchanges have been played at a high tempo, as you'd expect of any derby game.
Gomes presses high to steal possession for Wolves, before seeing a shot clatter off his own man and behind for a goal kick.
Wolves have won three of their last four Premier League games against Villa (one draw in January), as many as in their first 12 against them beforehand (four draws, five defeats).
Toti's goal was the difference when these teams last met here in May.
Villa enjoyed most of the possession early on, with Wolves sitting back in their 3-4-3 shape.
The hosts are enjoying a better spell on the ball now, however.
Gomes finds Neto with a searching pass out to the right, and the in-form winger skips past McGinn before being fouled by the Scot.
Wolves have a free-kick near the right corner of the box, which Neto looks set to deliver into the penalty area.
After some more pushing and pulling leads to another talking-to from the referee, Neto delivers his free-kick towards Toti at the back.
It's just too high for the Portuguese defender, however, and it runs out of play.
Over! Diaby faces up to Ait-Nouri on the right of the Wolves box before picking out McGinn on the edge of the D.
He has space and time to shoot, but he lifts his effort comfortably over Sa's goal.
Konsa drives forward to win a corner on the Villa right.
It's cleared and Wolves break through the energetic Cunha, who crosses behind off Diego Carlos for a corner at the other end.
McGinn has gone down holding his face under absolutely no contact from Dawson, as the players await the set-piece delivery.
It's far to say the Molineux crowd aren't taking kindly to that.
Neto's delivery is overhit, but Gomes keeps it alive and Wolves eventually win another set-piece as Konsa clears behind ahead of Dawson.
Now Dawson is down in the box ahead of the corner being taken.
Referee Robert Jones has yet another conversation with those involved before Neto swings the set-piece in... and beyond everyone.
Semedo looks for the run of Hwang with a cute ball in behind, but it's just cut out ahead of the South Korea star.
This is a better spell for the hosts, who started slowly.
Hwang has scored five of Wolves' last nine Premier League goals.
Nine of his overall 12 goals in the competition have either drawn Wolves level (two) or put them one goal ahead (seven).
Can he make another telling contribution here?
Cash wins possession from Ait-Nouri before looking for Watkins' run in behind the home defence, but captain Kilman comes across to make a crucial interception and stop the attack at source.
Dawson goes into the book now, stepping out of defence to challenge Watkins from behind and catching the Villa striker's heel.
It's definitely a hybrid system for Villa, with Konsa, Diego Carlos and Torres spreading wide as a back three in certain spells of possession.
In other moments, Digne drops in and Konsa pushes across to right-back, allowing Cash to play high.
McGinn goes into the book for catching Neto late on the touchline, leaving the winger in a heap off the pitch.
McGinn and Dawson have been getting stuck in so far, but now both men are walking a disciplinary tightrope.
We're past the half-hour mark on Molineux, and it's been a start high on intensity and application but low on quality in the final third.
Cash's early volley – kept out by Sa – remains the best chance.
Villa have lost five of their last six away games against Wolves in the Premier League and the Championship, winning the other 1-0 in the 2020-21 Premier League season, behind closed doors.
CHANCE! Lemina wins possession on the edge of Villa's box before offloading to Hwang on his left.
Hwang drives a low cross into Ait-Nouri, who just gets too much whip on his finish and sees it bend away from the far corner.
That's Wolves' best opening yet.
Ait-Nouri is down and in need of treatment on halfway following a collision with Cash.
The Villa man's shoulder appeared to crash into Ait-Nouri's face.
There was no ill intent, but it's a painful one.
Both coaches take the chance to pass on instructions to their players as Ait-Nouri continues to receive medical attention.
The Algeria international is now back on his feet.
Ait-Nouri will have to leave the pitch momentarily, but it looks like he's going to play on.
Wolves restart the game, temporarily playing with 10 men.
Villa win a free-kick deep inside their own half and Ait-Nouri can re-enter the field of play.
Semedo catches Digne with a high foot on halfway and concedes a free-kick.
On second viewing, both men had raised their boots and there was little real contact.
There referee opts against brandishing a card.
The game is becoming stretched now as Kilman shows excellent composure to feed Lemina, who advances across halfway.
He eventually loses possession, however, and Cunha breaks up the counter-attack with a tactical foul.
Diego Carlos advances forward from the back but becomes frustrated by a lack of movement, gesticulating furiously at his team-mates.
McGinn goes over the top to Digne, but Kilman comes across to halt his advance.
Villa are gifted a corner as Luiz's volley takes a massive deflection before looping high into the air.
It takes a big bounce upon landing, preventing Sa from keeping it in play.
CHANCE! The corner is only headed as far as Luiz, who lines up a shot from just inside the area.
He strikes it low, but two gold shirts converge on him to make a crucial block.
We're into a minimum of four minutes of first-half stoppage time, as McGinn shoves Semedo over to concede a foul in Wolves territory.
Hwang latches onto Kilman's outstanding pass over the top, but he's just forced out to the left side of the box.
He looks to volley it across with Neto and Cunha joining him, but Konsa makes the block and Villa clear the second ball.
HALF-TIME: WOLVES 0-0 ASTON VILLA.
The half-time whistle sounds at Molineux, and it's still goalless in this Midlands derby between Wolves and Aston Villa.
There has been plenty of effort from both teams, but neither has created much by way of clear-cut chances, with just one shot on target being recorded overall.
That came early on as Cash met McGinn's cross with a firm volley at the back post, only for Sa to keep it out.
Wolves have shown plenty of tenacity but struggled at the other end, with Ait-Nouri missing their best chance after good work from Lemina and Hwang.
More to come after the break!
Wolves have managed two shots to Villa's eight so far, failing to hit the target, though seven of the visitors' efforts have also been wayward, and half of them came from outside the area.
Both teams have been pretty risk-averse so far, but will that change as the game goes on? Don't go anywhere, we'll be back shortly.
Wolves have made a half-time substitution, likely an enforced one after Ait-Nouri's earlier head injury.
Doherty come on in a makeshift left wing-back role, with Hugo Bueno absent.
Villa get the ball rolling for the second half.
Can either team step things up in the final third after a pretty tame first 45 minutes?
SA DENIES WATKINS! Big chance for Villa as McGinn flashes a low cross into the path of Watkins.
An outstanding touch with the outside of his boot helps it goalwards, but Sa tips it over the top with an acrobatic stop!
Villa's resulting corner is cleared, then play stops as Hwang is caught and goes down with a head injury on the Wolves right.
Only Erling Haaland (23) and Harry Kane (17) have scored more Premier League goals than Watkins in 2023 (16).
He went so close to the opening goal there, but Sa made a brilliant reflex save!
Hwang is still down and receiving treatment after appearing to be caught with a flailing arm by Luiz.
It was certainly unintentional from the Villa man.
Hwang slowly climbs back to his feet.
He's been patched up after being caught on the nose, and he'll have to step off the pitch temporarily as Villa restart.
Cash takes advantage of a mix-up between Toti and Doherty at the far post to receive a high cross.
His volley goes straight into the ground and Dawson can help it over for a corner.
Over! McGinn's inswinging delivery is a decent one, but Luiz can't keep his header down from 10 yards out.

GOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLLLLLL!!! HWANG FOR WOLVES! 1-0! It's another goal for the South Korea international, and another assist for Neto! Neto receives a pass into feet just inside Villa's half before bursting past Torres to reach the byline.
He knocks a simple ball across the face of goal, and Hwang darts across the front post to tap it home!
That's Neto's fifth assist of the season, and it came from a run so similar to that which forced Ruben Dias' own goal last week!
GOOOOOOOOAAAAAALLL! TORRES LEVELS IMMEDIATELY! Wolves' lead did not last long! Villa win a deep free-kick, which is hoisted in by Luiz and only cleared as far as Watkins.
He digs out a first-time cross to the far post, where Torres slides in to poke it across goal and past Sa! 1-1!

events.action: poke it across goal and past Sa

text: Watkins has his second assist in as many Premier League games.
His left-footed cross was perfectly placed for Torres to bundle the ball home.
Out of absolutely nowhere, this game has burst into life.
We only had one shot on target in the first half, but we've seen two hit the net within 10 minutes of the restart.
Wolves win a free-kick in a crossing position on the left.
Neto's delivery is cleared but Wolves keep the pressure on and Diaby and Cash have to combine to stop another Neto cross.
Semedo steps ahead of Watkins to stop a long ball from floating in behind, then Dawson flies into a brilliant challenge to send the ball back towards Sa.
Watkins clatters into him as he does so and both players go down, but they're swiftly back to their feet and okay to continue.
Wolves aren't happy as Semedo is penalised for a challenge on McGinn, with the ball breaking neatly for Cunha after the Wolves wing-back appeared to make clean contact.
Villa can build from the free-kick.
Lemina goes into the book for a late challenge on McGinn in midfield.
Emery makes his first change and it comes in attack as Zaniolo replaces Diaby.
A deep free-kick from Luiz is nodded behind by Dawson with Diego Carlos lurking.
Villa win a corner on their left flank, but Luiz's delivery is headed out by Kilman at the far post.
Wolves goalscorer Hwang is down again, this time holding his throat following a collision involving Luiz off the ball.
We've just seen the replay, and Luiz unwisely pushed his hands into the attacker.
VAR will take a look at this incident...
NO RED CARD.
The VAR decides against advising a pitch-side review, which appears the right call as the contact was minimal.
However, Luiz took a risk by raising his hands and will be breathing a sigh of relief.
Wolves break in menacing fashion as Neto cuts inside from the right.
His low cross is cleared and Zaniolo can break, but Semedo hauls him down just short of the halfway line.
Semedo is booked for that foul on Zaniolo.
Strong play from Hwang, who escapes a tight position with some neat footwork to get Wolves moving forward.
Cunha is the target of a long ball forward, but Martinez can claim it untroubled.
O'Neil opts for a change in midfield, with Boubacar Traore replacing Gomes, who has been tidy here.
We're into the final 20 minutes of the 90 and this Midlands derby remains delicately poised.
Are there further twists and turns to come?
Neto charges between two challenges to enter the box before going down and throwing his arms aloft, but the referee is not interested in his protests.
He looked to go down somewhat softly with Diego Carlos and Kamara chasing him.
We've just seen that penalty appeal back, and there was very little in it.
It was another electrifying run from Neto, however.
What a season he's having!
HOW IS IT NOT 2-1?! Semedo breaks in behind and the flag surprisingly stays down.

He sends Torres down by rolling his studs over the ball, then shoots straight at Martinez on his weaker left foot! There was certainly a question of offside there, but he still should have put the ball in the net.
McGinn scoops a pass out to Digne, who keeps it in play to hook a cross into the area.
Boubacar Traore meets it with a booming clearance, sending two Villa players down and provoking protests from the away fans, but there was nothing in that.
O'Neil freshens up his attack now as towering striker Kalajdzic replaces Cunha.
Cunha, as ever, got through plenty of work off the ball in this game and helped drag his team up the pitch a few times.
The arrival of six-foot-seven striker Kalajdzic might signal a new approach from Wolves.
MASSIVE CHANCE FOR WOLVES! That should have been 2-1! Kalajdzic times his run to perfection to reach Hwang's pass in behind before sending an early low cross in for Neto.
Neto only has Martinez to beat, but he lifts his rushed attempt over on his weaker right foot.
Big let-off for Villa!
Emery is about to make some changes as we enter the final 10 minutes of regular time.
Bailey is one of two Villa substitutes preparing to enter the action.
The home fans appeal for handball as Watkins brings down a long pass forwards, but the referee declines to blow his whistle.
Watkins gets into the area before seeing his cross cut out by Kilman, but Kalajdzic subsequently concedes a free-kick in the right-back position.
Bailey comes on in place of Cash on the Villa right.
Tielemans is also sent on, with Kamara making way.
McGinn's free-kick is delivered nicely with Diego Carlos attacking it, but it's a gold shirt that gets there first to clear.
Chance! Wolves break through Neto once again.
This time, he cuts inside before offloading to Kaladjzic, whose shot lacks power and is blocked by a white shirt.
Lemina then goes for goal from range, but Martinez can fall on it to his left.
There's a brief stoppage now with both Hwang and Zaniolo down.
Zaniolo looks like he'll attempt to continue, but Silva looks set to replace the Wolves goalscorer from the bench.
Silva replaces Hwang as O'Neil makes his fourth substitution.
We're into the last five minutes here as Villa restart the game through Martinez, and it's still all to play for between these Midlands rivals!
Doherty steps inside after taking down Toti's pass before shaping to shoot... but a white shirt gets a foot in and Silva fouls Bailey as they contest the loose ball.
Kilman slices a clearance to give Zaniolo a second chance to cross from the left, but the Wolves captain recovers to block the delivery at source, then Zaniolo fouls Semedo in the corner.
The home fans are urging their team on as Traore almost intercepts a lax pass from Martinez.
Silva is then penalised for a foul as he looks to chase a long ball down the left channel.
Wow, we weren't expecting that! There will be 12 minutes of stoppage time at Molineux! Injuries to the likes of Hwang, Zaniolo and Ait-Nouri have contributed to that total.

BIG CHANCE! Watkins gets in behind Doherty inside the Wolves area before pulling the trigger... but he only hits the side netting! There's a brief VAR check to ascertain whether Doherty clipped the England striker, but that is swiftly cleared.
RED CARD FOR LEMINA! WOLVES ARE DOWN TO 10 MEN! Lemina surges over halfway before mistiming a pass towards Neto, allowing Zaniolo to intercept.
The Italian darts forward, and Lemina is penalised for pulling him back by his shorts.
The referee has no choice but to show a second yellow card!
Luiz sends a wild 30-yard strike well wide.
Villa still have seven minutes to play against numerically depleted opponents – can they make it count?
Lemina received a good ovation from the Wolves fans as he embarked on the long walk to the dressing room.
He will miss Wolves' trip to Bournemouth after the international break, though he would have done so regardless of his second booking after bringing up five for the season with his first.
Wolves are struggling to hold onto the ball since Lemina's red card.
Neto is filling in as an auxiliary midfielder as O'Neil has used up his three substitution windows.
We've got four minutes to go as Villa patiently probe for an opening.
McGinn holds off his man to tee up Luiz, but a Wolves shirt gets their to block his low effort.
That was a huge intervention! Corner for Villa.
SO CLOSE! The corner is flicked on to the back post, where Zaniolo hooks a right-footed volley back across goal.
Sa is rooted to the spot... but it just rolls wide of the bottom-right corner!
Semedo takes his time over a throw-in on the right, before committing a foul throw! The ball is back with Villa as we enter the last two minutes of stoppage time.
BIG SAVE FROM SA! McGinn backs into Toti to hold the ball up for Luiz, who finds Digne to his left.
The Frenchman cuts it back for Konsa, whose left-footed finish is blocked by the Wolves goalkeeper!
OFF THE POST! INCREDIBLE! Watkins almost wins it with the last touch of the game! The referee lets the contest tick into the 103rd minute as Digne crosses from the left.
It's a beautiful delivery which is nodded downwards by Watkins, and it bounces off the base of the post! Wolves escape with a point.
FULL-TIME: WOLVES 1-1 ASTON VILLA.
Yellow Card Saša Kalajdžić

The referee blows for full-time, and 10-man Wolves survive a Villa onslaught to take a point from this fiercely contested Midlands derby at Molineux! Villa missed the only real chance of a drab first half as Sa denied Cash, but the game exploded into life after the restart.
Another incredible solo run from Neto allowed Hwang to put Wolves ahead, but that lead was short-lived as Torres prodded in the equaliser.
Watkins and Neto exchanged misses before Lemina put Wolves' hopes in danger with a second yellow card in stoppage time, and Wolves had to ride their luck through 12 additional minutes.
Sa denied Konsa from close range, then Watkins headed against the post at the death.
A dramatic game finishes all square!
That result takes Wolves to eight points from as many games to kick off the 2023-24 season, a tally O'Neil may be content with given his team have already played five of last term's top seven.
They are 14th going into the international break, while Villa are fifth with 16 points, above Brighton on goal difference after the Seagulls drew 2-2 with Liverpool.
We hope you've enjoyed our coverage of another hard-fought Premier League encounter.
It's goodbye from us for now, and we'll see you next time!
